hero.name: Oleksii Odarchuk
hero.tagline: I build systems where speed meets architectural reliability.
hero.intro: Product-minded engineer. I turn ideas into services in hours — from hackathon MVPs to production-ready Go services. Off the clock — designing my own programming language.

about.title: About me
about.p1: I'm a Go backend engineer, second-year student at Lviv Polytechnic IT College. I build systems where every millisecond counts and the architecture survives both load and shifting requirements.
about.p2: Outside of code: 10+ years of folk dancing, occasional poetry, and recently — screenwriting. That taught me rhythm and structure — the things every good product is built on.

achievements.title: Wins & hackathons
achievements.subtitle: Not just code — outcomes measured in places, speed, and offers.

best.label: 🏆 1st place
best.title: BEST Hackathon
best.description: Algorithm to reconstruct a UAV's trajectory without GPS — from IMU, barometer and other inertial-sensor logs. Sensor fusion in Go + C, clean modular architecture (telemetry / integration / simulation). The judges singled out the architectural resilience — 1st place among top teams.

mate.label: 🥉 3rd place
mate.title: Mate Hackathon
mate.description: Designed and built a Go backend from scratch in 7 hours for an AI-powered competitor-ad analysis tool. Dual AI pipeline: GPT-4o (triggers) + Nano Banano 2 / fal.ai (creative generation). Beat teams with 5+ years of experience by shipping a stable MVP.

dou.label: 🎟 Invitation
dou.title: DOU Day 2026
dou.description: Personally invited by the organisers to DOU Day with a free ticket as a student with high potential. Dedicated track for promising student developers.

security.label: 🛡 Disclosure → offer
security.title: Security Researcher
security.description: Found and exploited a critical vulnerability: the frontend capped transaction amounts, the backend didn't — enabling arbitrary negative-value transfers. Disclosed responsibly, got a job offer from the admins. Reverse-engineered the official JS miner via Webpack bundles and rewrote it in Go with a goroutine pool — 1000× faster.

projects.title: Selected projects
projects.subtitle: What I build off-hours — and what I'm proud of.

piton.name: Piton
piton.tagline: A Ukrainian programming language with a homegrown interpreter
piton.description: A lightweight interpreted language with an authentic Ukrainian syntax (in transliteration). Recursive descent parser, tree-walking evaluator, native SVG flowchart generation, Turing-complete. Written from scratch in Go, no yacc/bison. The interpreter is compiled to WebAssembly via TinyGo — 220 KB instead of 24 MB, runs entirely in the browser.

shminer.title: SHMiner
shminer.subtitle: Desktop crypto miner
shminer.description: Cross-platform miner on Wails (Go + Svelte/TS). Rewrote SHA-256 from JS to Go with a goroutine worker pool — 1000× faster hashrate on identical hardware. AES-encrypted wallet, real-time WebSocket dashboard, multi-wallet, zen mode.

linkshortener.title: LinkShortener Bot
linkshortener.subtitle: Telegram + analytics
linkshortener.description: Telegram URL shortener with QR generation and geo-analytics. PostgreSQL for storage, Redis for redirect cache, ClickHouse for real-time click analytics (country, city, platform). Docker, GeoIP2.

todolist.title: ToDoList Pro
todolist.subtitle: Production-grade task manager
todolist.description: Go/Gin backend with clean architecture (repository → service → handler), JWT + OAuth 2.0 (Google), email verification, Swagger docs. Svelte 5 + TypeScript + Tailwind. Multi-stage Docker build.

abit.title: AbitAssistant Bot
abit.subtitle: Telegram bot for applicants
abit.description: Helps Ukrainian students track university admission rankings. Reverse-engineered closed third-party APIs. 150+ active users in the first year, marketing campaign planned for 2026.

lab.title: Piton Lab — try my language
lab.subtitle: The interpreter is compiled to WebAssembly via TinyGo — ~220 KB. The flowchart engine is a separate ~5 MB brotli module (full D2 engine), lazy-loaded only when you actually need a chart.
lab.loadHint: Hit "Run" — the interpreter loads on first interaction (~220 KB).
